clue.text: Accusation in glib eloquent fashion

indicators.note: in tells the solver the letters sit inside the run of words glib eloquent

explanation.surface: Someone makes a charge smoothly and persuasively.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between 'glib' and 'eloquent'; 'fashion' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Libel is a published false statement damaging someone, so it is a kind of accusation.

clue.text: Pointless communication?

parts.note: pointless reads as a tennis score of no points, love, and a communication is a letter sent through the post

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointless' suggests futile, but in tennis a score of nil is love.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic note to a sweetheart is a message of affection, with love meaning zero in tennis.

clue.text: Stop a humble building

parts.note: a bung is a stopper
low means lowly or humble

explanation.surface: Someone halts a modest structure.
explanation.definitionFit: A bungalow is a one-storey house, a type of building.

clue.text: Left relative who did not start the hilarity

indicators.note: who did not start says the relative loses its first letter

parts.note: a daughter is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member who walked away was not the one who began the fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who did not start' removes the D from DAUGHTER, leaving AUGHTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the sound of mirth, the outward sign of hilarity.

clue.text: Spotted having kiss in toboggan

indicators.note: in says the word for kiss goes inside the word for toboggan

parts.note: a toboggan is a sled
a peck is a quick kiss

explanation.surface: Someone was seen snogging on a sledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' reads as 'seen', but it is the adjective meaning dotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Speckled and spotted both describe a surface covered with small marks.

clue.text: Thus us barman has to add this to whisky

parts.note: so means thus, in that way
a district attorney, DA, is an American lawyer, a member of the bar

explanation.surface: An American bartender has to put a mixer in a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barman' is not a bartender but a lawyer called to the bar; in the US a district attorney is a DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is the classic mixer for a Scotch, as in whisky and soda.

clue.text: Bone male bird number six reportedly found

indicators.note: reportedly means the words are judged by how they are heard

parts.note: a cock is a male bird, followed by six

explanation.surface: A bone from a rooster numbered six has been found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' says COCK and SIX together sound like the bone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The coccyx is the small triangular bone at the base of the spine, the tailbone.

clue.text: Us immigrant from Los Angeles can take nothing

parts.note: a tin is a can
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An American newcomer from LA manages with nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb but is the noun, a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Latino describes a person of Latin American origin living in the United States.

clue.text: Drug found inside parched nest

indicators.note: found inside says the drug is placed within the word for parched

parts.note: parched means dry
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Narcotics are discovered in an arid hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: A drey is a squirrel's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: A drey is the twiggy home a squirrel builds in a tree.

clue.text: Dared to have used this capital before day begins

indicators.note: before places the word for the capital ahead of the letter from day

parts.note: venture capital is money invested in a new business, so the word that goes before capital

indicators.note: begins asks for only the opening letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Someone risked money in a start-up just as the day began.
explanation.walkthrough: VENTURE comes from the phrase venture capital, funding put into risky new firms; 'day begins' gives D.
explanation.definitionFit: To venture is to take a risk, so ventured means had the nerve or dared.

clue.text: Clay Rita modelled with cheerful readiness

indicators.note: modelled means shaped like clay, so the letters of clay rita are moulded into a new order

explanation.surface: A girl called Rita happily shapes some clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity is eager willingness, a brisk and cheerful promptness.

clue.text: Unlikely to appeal to schoolchildren for a considerable time

definitions.meaning: pupils would dislike an extended stretch of school between holidays
lasting or planned over an extended period

explanation.walkthrough: A school year in Britain is split into terms; a long one would not please pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-term means extending far into the future, covering a lengthy period.

clue.text: Edward hides the hide

indicators.note: hides says the word the is concealed inside the surname

parts.note: Edward Lear was the Victorian nonsense poet

explanation.surface: A man named Edward conceals an animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward stands for LEAR, after Edward Lear, writer of nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussycat. 'Hides' then 'hide' play on the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Leather is tanned animal hide, the skin of a beast prepared for use.

clue.text: Refer to surprising inclusion of round ridgepole

indicators.note: inclusion of says the round letter is taken inside the other letters
surprising suggests the letters of refer to turn out in an unexpected order

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone is pointed to an unexpected round pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprising' rearranges REFER TO to ROFTREE, and 'inclusion of' slips O in after the first O.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooftree is the horizontal beam along the ridge of a roof, also called a ridgepole.

clue.text: Alumnus criticises said debts that are offensive

parts.note: an alumnus is a former pupil, an old boy, abbreviated OB

indicators.note: said means the word for criticises is heard rather than written

parts.note: to knock something is to criticise it
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debts

explanation.surface: A former pupil complains about money people owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' tells you to spell KNOCKS by how it is heard, giving NOX; OB (old boy) is the British term for a school alumnus.
explanation.definitionFit: Obnoxious means highly unpleasant or objectionable, hence offensive.

clue.text: Volume of students?

parts.note: reads as a quantity of pupils, but means a textbook used by pupils

explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' tempts as a crowd size or loudness, but it is a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A textbook used in class is a book belonging to pupils, a volume for learners.

clue.text: Horse pulling barge, one is reliable

definitions.meaning: a horse that tows a barge along a canal is a strong tower, one who tows
a dependable person who gives support in trouble

explanation.surface: A canal horse hauling its boat is praised as dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer's first word as TOW-ER, one who tows, a horse of great strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A person you can lean on in a crisis is called a solid source of support; the barge horse is a strong tow-er.

clue.text: Still decline after the end of the afternoon

parts.note: even can mean still, as in even better
a fall is a decline

explanation.surface: A downturn persists after the afternoon ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Evenfall is a poetic word for dusk, the close of day when evening comes on.

clue.text: Daily with minor responsibilities

definitions.meaning: a daily newspaper, here the British national paper
a person legally in charge of a child under age

explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is a British daily newspaper; 'minor' means a child, not 'small'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Guardian is a national daily paper, and a legal guardian looks after a minor.

clue.text: Recorder found main point during rarer excitement

indicators.note: during says the main point goes in the middle of the other letters
excitement stirs up the letters of rarer into a new order

parts.note: the gist is the main point of something

explanation.surface: Someone discovers the key thing amid unusual thrills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' suggests a flute or a tape machine, but here it is the official who keeps records; 'excitement' is the anagram signal and 'during' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A registrar is an official who keeps records, such as of births and marriages.

clue.text: Gary interminably licked half of pungent root

indicators.note: interminably means without end, so the name loses its last letter
half of takes the first three of the six letters of licked

explanation.surface: Gary kept licking a strong-tasting bulb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminably' trims Y from GARY; 'half of' takes LIC from LICKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Garlic is a strong-smelling bulb used as a flavouring, loosely called a root.

clue.text: Sergeant-major includes it with company programme

indicators.note: includes says the other pieces go inside the abbreviation for the sergeant-major

explanation.surface: A senior soldier adds something to the unit's schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'programme' is a TV show here, not a plan of events.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitcom, situation comedy, is a type of television show.

clue.text: Water that is crystalline in form!

definitions.meaning: as in ... water from a spring
a naturally occurring solid such as quartz with a crystal structure

explanation.definitionFit: Mineral water is bottled spring water, and a mineral is a natural inorganic solid usually of crystal structure.

clue.text: Lady put articles behind broken door

indicators.note: behind puts the articles after the rearranged door
broken shows the letters of door are smashed into another order

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

explanation.surface: A woman puts some items behind a damaged door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' signals the anagram of the door, and 'behind' places the two articles after it, so the woman's name is built back to front from the surface's order.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothea is a woman's first name, as in Dorothea Brooke of Middlemarch.

clue.text: Lady stops short of podium

indicators.note: stops short means the name ends one letter early

parts.note: Daisy is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman halts just before reaching the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops short' cuts the last letter off DAISY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dais is a raised platform for a speaker, like a podium.

clue.text: One outspoken lady

indicators.note: outspoken means the word for one is spoken out loud

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A single woman who speaks her mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outspoken' looks like frank, but means said out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne is a woman's name, so a lady.

clue.text: Had nothing more than stew during battle

indicators.note: more than here means added on top, the nothing coming after the stew

parts.note: navarin is a French stew of lamb or mutton
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Soldiers ate only stew while fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: NAVARIN is a French lamb stew; the Battle of Navarino (1827) was a naval battle in the Greek War of Independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Navarino was an 1827 naval engagement off Greece, so it names a battle.

clue.text: Thus, say, am finding raw material behind tree

indicators.note: behind puts the raw material after the other pieces
say means the word for thus is spelt by how it is heard

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
ore is the raw material mined for metal

explanation.surface: Someone explains where they find the raw stuff for timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' makes the Latin word sound like the first syllable of the tree; 'behind' puts the mined raw stuff last. SIC is used in print to mark a quotation as written.
explanation.definitionFit: The sycamore is a large broadleaved tree of the maple family.

clue.text: Mistakenly link up most of spaceship

indicators.note: mistakenly says the letters are put together wrongly, so rearranged
most of drops the last letter of the word up

explanation.surface: Someone wrongly joins up a large part of a spacecraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims UP to U; 'Mistakenly' rearranges LINK plus U.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunik was the name given to early Soviet lunar probes, unmanned spacecraft sent to the Moon.
